scheme_name: Financial Assistance for Education- Haryana Silicosis Board
description:
The Financial Assistance for Education scheme under the Haryana Silicosis Board is a targeted initiative aimed at providing educational support to the children of individuals affected by silicosis in the state of Haryana.

The scheme was launched in the year 2016 as part of the Haryana Silicosis Board's broader efforts to address the health and socio-economic challenges faced by families impacted by this occupational disease.

Silicosis is a progressive lung disease caused by inhaling fine silica dust, primarily affecting workers in industries such as mining and stone crushing.

The primary objective of the Financial Assistance for Education scheme is to ensure that the children of silicosis-affected families receive quality education without financial constraints.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to eligible students from class 1 to post-graduate levels.

The financial assistance under this scheme is structured to cover various educational expenses including tuition fees, books, and other necessary materials.

For students in primary and secondary education, the scheme provides a financial assistance amount of INR 10,000 per annum.

For students pursuing higher education, the assistance amount increases to INR 15,000 per annum.

The assistance is intended to alleviate the financial burden on families who have lost their primary breadwinner due to silicosis.

Eligibility for the scheme is specifically targeted at the children of workers who have been diagnosed with silicosis.

To qualify, the applicant must be a child of a silicosis-affected worker who is registered with the Haryana Silicosis Board.

There are no specific age limits set for the children applying for this scheme.

However, the educational qualifications must align with the levels of assistance being sought.

For instance, students must be enrolled in recognized educational institutions to be eligible for the financial assistance.

The application process for the Financial Assistance for Education scheme is straightforward and designed to be accessible.

Interested applicants must fill out the application form available on the official Haryana Silicosis Board website.

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, age, educational institution, and the details of the silicosis-affected parent.

Additionally, applicants must submit a copy of the silicosis diagnosis certificate issued by a competent medical authority.

Proof of enrollment in the educational institution is also required to validate the claim for financial assistance.

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the local office of the Haryana Silicosis Board.

The processing of applications typically takes around 30 days from the date of submission.

Disbursement of funds is carried out directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.

The financial assistance is disbursed on an annual basis to ensure that students have the necessary funds at the beginning of the academic year.

The Haryana Silicosis Board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment of the Government of Haryana.

For any inquiries or assistance regarding the scheme, individuals can contact the Haryana Silicosis Board at their official helpline number.

The helpline number is available on the Haryana Silicosis Board's official website for easy access.

In terms of outreach, the Haryana Silicosis Board has conducted awareness programs to inform affected families about the financial assistance available.

As of 2023, the scheme has benefited thousands of students across Haryana.

The Haryana Silicosis Board has reported that over 5,000 students have received financial assistance since the scheme's inception.

This assistance has played a crucial role in enabling these students to continue their education despite the financial hardships faced by their families.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare measures aimed at improving the living conditions of workers and their families in Haryana.

The Haryana government has allocated a budget of INR 5 crores for the Financial Assistance for Education scheme for the financial year 2023-2024.

This budget allocation reflects the government's commitment to supporting the education of children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

The scheme also aligns with the national objective of promoting education for all, especially for marginalized communities.

The Haryana Silicosis Board continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Regular audits and assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the financial assistance on students' educational outcomes.

The board also collaborates with educational institutions to facilitate the smooth disbursement of funds and to ensure that students are aware of their entitlements.

In addition to financial assistance, the Haryana Silicosis Board provides counseling and support services to families affected by silicosis.

This holistic approach aims to address not only the educational needs but also the emotional and psychological challenges faced by these families.

The Financial Assistance for Education scheme is a vital component of the Haryana government's efforts to combat the adverse effects of silicosis on workers and their families.

By providing financial support for education, the scheme helps to break the cycle of poverty and improve the socio-economic status of affected families.

The Haryana Silicosis Board is committed to ensuring that no child is deprived of education due to the financial constraints caused by silicosis.

The board regularly updates its policies and procedures to enhance the effectiveness of the scheme and to respond to the evolving needs of the community.

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance for Education scheme under the Haryana Silicosis Board represents a significant step towards empowering the children of silicosis-affected families through education.

This initiative not only provides financial relief but also fosters hope and opportunities for a better future for these children.
